text: National University of Computer & Emerging Sciences - NUCES - Karachi Department of Artificial Intelligence 6.1.1.3 The Limitation: The Anchored Origin This raises an important analytical question: Can this matric translate (slide) a point, such as moving (10, 20) to (110, 70)? The mathematical answer is no. A strict rule of linear transformations is that any matrix multiplied by a zero vector results in a zero vector : If you multiply the origin (@,@) by any 2 x 2 matrix, the result will always be . Because the origin is permanently anchored, standard linear transformations cannot translate geometry. They can spin, stretch, and shear the grid, but they cannot slide it across the board. This specific mathematical limitation is what forces computer graphics systems to introduce a workaround to achieve full affine transformations . The entire coordinate system is anchored at this single point. FAST NUCES - Karachi Talha Shahid 15
